newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Friday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed again today amid continued uncertainty over market direction. Treasury bill yields were steady to slightly higher but bond prices were slightly lower. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at a yield of 1.00/0.95 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 0.95/0.90 percent. One-year was unchanged from Thursday's yield of 1.50/1.45 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.15/99.20 against Thursday's close of S$99.16/99.21, September 2001 at S$97.35/97.40 versus S$97.36/97.41 and June 2003 at S$95.35/95.40 from S$95.36/95.41.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Thursday's 3-1/8 3 percent.
